content.title: Tired of viral '67' trend? In-N-Out is, too. Why burger chain banned order number
content.text: Updated Dec. 12, 2025, 3:48 p.m. ETDictionary.com announced its Word of the Year in October, and it's one that's been trending among youngsters.The word doesn't hold any true meaning, and is "impossible to define." However, that hasn't stopped the internet from using it. Instead, the word's ambiguity has only fueled its popularity on social media through memes and viral reels."Searches for '67'experienced a dramatic rise beginning in the summer of 2025. Since June, those searches have increased more than sixfold, and so far the surge shows no signs of stopping." said Dictionary.com, which selects its Word of the Year based on words that make an impact online and in real life conversations.Here's what to know about the internet slang that's been driving adults crazy.Where did the word '67' originate from?Brainrot term "67" (pronounced six seven) is believed to have originated from rapper Skrilla's song "Doot Doot (67)," according to Dictionary.com. Like wildfire, the word was quick to spread through viral Tik Toks featuring basketball players and a boy known as the "67 Kid.""Within weeks, teachers were trading tips online about how to get their students to stop saying '67' all day long." said Dictionary.com.What does '67' mean?Adults may think there is a deeper meaning to the word "67," but those who have been waiting for this mystery to be revealed may be disappointed (or relieved).There is speculation the word "67" is just another way to say "so-so" or "maybe this, maybe that." There is also a hand gesture to go along with the term where both palms are facing upwards and move up and down alternatively. Some kids use the term in reply to any given question just to bug their elders."It’s meaningless, ubiquitous, and nonsensical. In other words, it has all the hallmarks of brainrot." Dictionary.com said. "It’s the logical endpoint of being perpetually online, scrolling endlessly, consuming content fed to users by algorithms trained by other algorithms. And what are we left with in the wake of this relentless sensory overload? 67."Why was '67' banned from In-N-Out Burger?West Coast burger chain In-N-Out is not a fan of the "67" trend and has removed the order number from its ticket systems due to videos that went viral at some of its restaurants.According to People, removal of order number "67" was discovered on Reddit, where one user commented "while i was at work yesterday night, i noticed that everytime i would get to number 66, and then get to the next customer it would just go to number 68, an it would skip 67. now im curious on if or why they removed it."In this Instagram compilation video, crowds of excited teenagers can been seen waiting at In-N-Out front counters. When the order "67" is called, youngsters begin jumping up and down, recording with their cell phones as they holler at the top of their lungs in celebration of what they deem as the restaurant's acknowledgment of the viral trend.To avoid disruptions like this from occurring in the future, In-N-Out decided to yank the order number from its ticket systems altogether. Other restaurants saw the "67" trend as a way to cash in, like Wendy's, who offered frosties for 67 cents for a limited time. Pizza Hut also had a promotion where they offered 67 cent boneless wings on Nov. 6 and 7.Nina Tran covers trending topics for The Greenville News, part of the USA TODAY Network. Reach her via email at ntran@usatodayco.com.
